summary: Node id declared twice with different labels
help: Give each node one label, or use a new id for the second node.
rationale: Mermaid keeps one of the two declarations and drops the other, so the rendered diagram is wrong.

summary: The legacy graph header keyword; flowchart is the current form and enables per-subgraph direction
help: Write flowchart instead of graph as the header keyword.
rationale: graph is the legacy spelling, and newer features such as subgraph direction work only under flowchart.

summary: flowchart or graph header without a direction; the layout silently defaults to TD
help: Add a direction such as TD or LR after the header keyword.
rationale: An omitted direction hides an implicit default, so writing it makes the reading order explicit.

summary: The same edge is declared more than once, so the duplicates render stacked
help: Remove the repeated edge statement, or give the edges different labels.
rationale: Repeated edges stack on top of each other and are usually a copy-paste mistake.

summary: A node has an edge to itself, such as A --> A; this is almost always unintended
help: Point the edge at the node that was meant, or remove it.
rationale: A self-loop is rarely intentional in a flowchart and usually points at a typo in one endpoint.

summary: A node label is empty, such as A[]; it renders as a blank shape
help: Write text inside the brackets, or drop the brackets and use the bare node id.
rationale: An empty label draws a shape with no text, which usually means a missing label.

summary: A node is declared but never connected by an edge
help: Connect the node to the graph with an edge, or remove its declaration.
rationale: Subgraph-only members legitimately have no edges, so this rule is off by default.

summary: The same node id is declared more than once with the same label
help: Declare each node once; later declarations are usually copy-paste noise.
rationale: Mermaid merges the declarations, so the extra lines only add confusion.

summary: A click statement names a local relative file path that does not exist beside the input
help: Use a target file that exists, or an http, https, or mailto link.
rationale: The predicate reads files beside the input.
reason: reads files beside the input, and the core does no I/O

summary: A single arrow -> is used in a flowchart
help: Replace -> with -->, or use -- text --> for an inline label.
rationale: Mermaid flowcharts require the double arrow, so a single arrow does not connect the nodes.

summary: An inline link uses a one-sided end marker, such as --x--> or --o-->
help: Use a symmetric marker pair such as x--x, or a plain arrow with a label.
rationale: Mermaid supports markers only on both ends of a link, so a one-sided marker is dropped.

summary: A node label contains a backslash-escaped quote, which Mermaid does not support
help: Use " for the inner quotes instead of a backslash escape.
rationale: Mermaid has no backslash escape inside labels, so the backslash reaches the output.

summary: A double-quoted label contains another double quote
help: Use " for the inner quotes.
rationale: The second double quote ends the label early and corrupts the rest of the line.

summary: A single-quoted label contains an unescaped double quote
help: Replace the inner double quote with ", or use a double-quoted label with " inside.
rationale: Mermaid mis-parses a bare double quote inside a single-quoted label.

summary: A node label contains a backtick
help: Remove the backticks and keep the text.
rationale: Backticks have no meaning in a flowchart label and reach the output verbatim.

summary: A double quote appears inside an unquoted label
help: Wrap the whole label in double quotes and write inner quotes as ".
rationale: A bare quote inside an unquoted label ends parsing early and breaks the statement.

summary: The header lacks a direction after flowchart or graph
help: Add a direction such as TD, TB, BT, RL, or LR after the header keyword.
rationale: Without a direction the layout picks one silently, which may not match the intent.

summary: The direction token after the header is not one of TD, TB, BT, RL, LR
help: Use one of TD, TB, BT, RL, or LR.
rationale: An unknown direction token is ambiguous and no automatic replacement exists.

summary: An unknown keyword appears before the direction token
help: Replace the unknown keyword with direction.
rationale: Only direction introduces an explicit direction, so another keyword cannot be interpreted.

summary: Two nodes appear on one line without a connecting arrow
help: Insert --> between the two nodes.
rationale: A line with two bare node ids is not a valid statement and the edge never renders.

summary: A meta statement such as title appears in a flowchart
help: Use a Markdown heading above the block, or draw a labelled node at the top.
rationale: The flowchart grammar has no title statement, so the line is dropped.

summary: end appears without a matching subgraph
help: Remove this end line, or add a subgraph above it.
rationale: A stray end breaks the block structure and the parser loses track of the subgraphs.

summary: A node shape opens but is never closed
help: Add the matching closing bracket, for example A[Label].
rationale: An unclosed bracket swallows the rest of the line and misparses the diagram.

summary: The opening and closing brackets of a node shape do not match
help: Close with the bracket that matches the opener, for example ) for (.
rationale: Mismatched brackets leave the shape unterminated and the statement misparses.

summary: A node shape has empty content, such as A[]
help: Write text inside the brackets, or drop the brackets and use the bare node id.
rationale: An empty shape draws no visible label, which usually means a missing one.

summary: A node label opens a quote but never closes it
help: Close the quote, for example A["Label"].
rationale: The rest of the line is read as label text until the parser gives up.

summary: A class statement is missing node ids or the class name
help: Write class A,B classname.
rationale: Both parts are required, and guessing them needs the author's intent.

summary: subgraph is not followed by an id or a [Title]
help: Write subgraph apiId [API Layer].
rationale: A subgraph without a header has no identity, and choosing one needs the author's intent.

summary: A node label is not quoted, which strict mode requires
help: Wrap the label in double quotes and write inner quotes as ".
rationale: The rule exists only for maid's strict mode.
reason: it applies in strict mode only, and this project has no strict mode

summary: linkStyle references an edge id that no link defines
help: Attach the id to a link first, as in e1@-->, before styling it.
rationale: Styling a nonexistent edge id changes nothing, so the statement is dead.

summary: An edge attribute statement such as e1@{ ... } names an edge id that no link defines
help: Attach the id to a link first, as in A e1@--> B.
rationale: Attributes for a nonexistent edge id change nothing, so the statement is dead.

summary: An unquoted label contains an opening or closing parenthesis
help: Wrap the label in double quotes, or replace ( and ) with ( and ).
rationale: Parentheses look like a shape delimiter, so the label misparses without quotes.

summary: A click call statement carries tooltip or target text after call fn()
help: Write click A call doThing() with no trailing text.
rationale: Mermaid rejects text after call(), so the extra words make the statement invalid.

summary: A class statement applies to a node id that the diagram never defines
help: Define the node before applying classes, or move the class line below the node.
rationale: A class on a nonexistent node silently changes nothing.

summary: A style statement targets a node id that the diagram never defines
help: Define the node before styling it, or move the style line below the node.
rationale: A style on a nonexistent node silently changes nothing.

summary: The linkStyle style pairs are placed on a line after the indices
help: Put the styles on the same line as the indices, for example linkStyle 0,1 stroke:red.
rationale: Styles on a following line are not attached to the indices and are dropped.

summary: A range such as 0:3 is used in the linkStyle index list
help: Use comma-separated indices instead, for example linkStyle 0,1,2.
rationale: Mermaid accepts no index ranges in linkStyle, so the statement misparses.

summary: A typed shape in an @{ shape: ... } node is not supported
help: Use one of the supported shape names such as rect, rounded, diamond, or circle.
rationale: The named shape is unknown, so the node cannot be drawn as asked.

summary: An unquoted label contains an at sign
help: Wrap the whole label in double quotes, for example B["@scope/package v1.0"].
rationale: The at sign starts attribute syntax such as @{ shape: ... } and e1@-->, so an unquoted label that holds one can be misparsed.

summary: A node id inside a subgraph repeats the id of an enclosing subgraph
help: Rename the node or the subgraph, or give the subgraph a quoted title with no explicit id.
rationale: One id then names a subgraph and one of its own members, which makes the subgraph contain itself.
